name: KY-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: Deeply Republican district with R+18 partisan lean
Prediction markets price Democratic win at about 2 percent
Democratic nominee is minimally funded with no outside support
Open seat after Massie lost renomination, but GOP nominee heavily backed
model.rationale: This northern Kentucky seat is strongly Republican, and the Democratic nominee has raised under $100,000 with no outside spending while the GOP nominee benefited from millions in outside support. Markets price a Republican win near certainty, so the only real question is the size of the margin.
model.watch: Any unexpected scandal involving the Republican nominee or a surge of Democratic outside spending could narrow the margin, though a Democratic win remains highly unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Thomas Massie (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Kentucky's 4th District is a heavily Republican seat, and Thomas Massie's departure after losing renomination does not change the partisan fundamentals. Ed Gallrein won the Republican nomination with substantial outside backing, both supporting and opposing spending in the millions, reflecting an expensive primary fight.

Melissa Strange, the Democratic nominee, has raised only about $94,000 and has no outside support, while a Libertarian is also on the ballot. Prediction markets give the Democrat roughly a 2 percent chance. The race is rated Safe Republican, with the main uncertainty being the exact margin rather than the winner.
